Choose the scenario for stepping through a run script by hand

Source: R/use_scenario.R
use_scenario.Rd

use_scenario() chooses the scenario and the simulation that every later initialize_project() call in this R session uses. It is for a person who steps through a run script by hand.

Usage

use_scenario(scenario, sim = 1)

Arguments

scenario

The scenario, one name of lower-case letters, digits and underscores. initialize_project() checks that it is in CFG$scenarios.

sim

The simulation, a whole number of 1 or more.

Value

Invisibly, a list with scenario and sim.

Details

Write one commented line for each scenario directly above the initialize_project() call of vNN_run.R, in the order of CFG$scenarios:

# Run one of these lines to step through a scenario by hand. The choice lasts for the R session.
# pbn::use_scenario("real", sim = 1)
# pbn::use_scenario("null", sim = 1)
p <- pbn::initialize_project(version = "v01", home = ".", data_raw = "/data/raw")

The rule use_scenario_lines of check_project() fails a run script that does not have exactly one such line for each scenario of CFG$scenarios, or that has a line for another scenario.

To step through a scenario, run one of these lines without the #, then run the script line by line. The lines MUST stay commented in the file. use_scenario() stops in a non-interactive R session, for example under Rscript, and check_project() fails an active call.

The choice lasts for the R session. Every later initialize_project() call uses it, also when you run that call again, until the next use_scenario() call. use_scenario("real", sim = 1) goes back to the real data. The command-line arguments scenario=<name> and sim=<k> replace the choice as a whole.

See also

Other project setup: end_if_fake_scenario(), initialize_project(), run_scenarios()

Examples

if (interactive()) {
  pbn::use_scenario("null", sim = 2)
}
